subject: Performance SLOs & context window - follow-up (FinCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Thomas <michael.thomas@finco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Performance SLOs & context window - follow-up (FinCo)

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Per our discovery call, I wanted to capture the performance / SLO items we discussed and the immediate next steps so we can scope a short benchmark and draft a mutual action plan. Below is my recap; please correct anything I got wrong.

Recap (what FinCo told us):
- Primary use case: real-time underwriting assistant embedded in customer-facing app.
- Typical request payload: 1-2 short documents (2-5 KB each) + user prompt; average input tokens estimated ~1.5k, peak up to ~6k for longer context.
- Desired output: concise decision summary (~200-400 tokens).
- Latency targets: 95th pct <= 400ms for simple prompts; 95th pct <= 800ms for heavy-context requests.
- Throughput & concurrency: initial target 150 concurrent sessions during peak with sustained throughput ~400 reqs/min; burst capacity to 1k concurrent for short windows.
- Streaming: client wants partial streaming for first-token feedback; must support server-sent events / chunked responses.
- Security: data residency kept in us-east region; SOC2 and audit logs required (we covered onboarding checklist).

Questions / items for us to validate (action items):
1) We need to validate whether the target latency numbers are achievable at the requested context window (6k input tokens + 400 output tokens) on our recommended model/quantization profile.
2) Confirm streaming latency (time-to-first-byte) expectations vs. end-to-end 95th latency SLO.
3) Provide a short benchmark plan: model variant(s) to test, hardware profile (GPU type), batching/concurrency config, and estimated cost.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood: produce an SLO matrix + benchmark plan (deliver by EOD Monday 16 Feb).
- FinCo: share two representative example prompts and one redacted long-context document for accuracy/latency simulation.
- Schedule a 30-min technical benchmark sync next week to review results and tradeoffs.

I attached a first-pass SLO matrix template (FinCo_SLO_matrix.pdf) and a link to the call recording. Laura / Rishi — I know you'll have notes on model choices and a proposed test harness.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window - follow-up (FinCo)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Everything looks correct. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- The 6k input token peak is primarily for monthly reports that get fed along with the prompt; critical user flows are usually in the 1-2k token range.
- For streaming: we'd like time-to-first-token (TTFT) < 200ms for simple requests; for heavy-context the TTFT can be up to ~350ms, but overall 95th end-to-end should still meet your numbers.
- Concurrency: the 1k concurrent burst would only be for < 10 minutes, but the 150 concurrent baseline is a hard requirement.

I'll upload two redacted example prompts and a long-context doc by EOD Friday (link to follow).

Also: is there any preliminary guidance you can share about quantization vs latency tradeoffs for large context sizes? Curious if 8-bit quantized variants materially change TTFT for 4-6k contexts.

Best,
Michael
Senior Product Manager — FinCo
michael.thomas@finco.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Performance SLOs & context window - follow-up (FinCo)

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick tech notes to seed the benchmark plan (I'll expand in the doc):

- Model family: recommend starting with an open 70B-ish encoder-decoder / decoder-only variant with solid context handling; prefer a model we've validated for streaming.
- Context handling: as context grows, KV-cache size increases linearly and impacts memory + time for each generation step. For 4-6k input tokens + 400 tokens output, expect per-token decode latency to increase ~15-30% vs. 1-2k context depending on kernel efficiency and GPU memory layout.
- Quantization: 8-bit (INT8) usually reduces memory footprint and can slightly improve throughput, but time-to-first-byte can be impacted if additional dequantization or custom kernels are required. Best to benchmark INT8 vs FP16 on the target GPU.
- Batching: continuous batching helps throughput but adds queuing latency. For a 95th SLO at 400ms we should keep per-request cross-request batching low (max batch size 4-8) or use per-session affinity to reduce variance.
- Streaming: we should measure TTFT separately. TTFT is mostly generator warmup + initial KV-materialization. With optimized kernels and pinned KV-cache, TTFT target ~120-200ms for 1-2k contexts; for 4-6k expect TTFT up to 300-350ms unless we use prefix caching.

Proposed benchmark matrix (short):
- Test A: FP16 on A100 80GB, single-request throughput, 1-2k context, measure 50/95/99 latencies, TTFT, and token/sec.
- Test B: FP16 on A100 80GB, 4-6k context.
- Test C: INT8 on same hardware for both context sizes.
- Test D: same tests but with simple batching (batch sizes 2,4,8) to simulate multiplexing.

I can prepare a harness that uses the sample prompts Michael will provide and run a small benchmark cluster. Need Rishi to confirm the recommended GPU flavor for Dedicated vs Hosted pricing comparison.

Laura
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window - follow-up (FinCo)

Michael —

Great — thanks for the clarifications and for uploading the examples. We pulled your files into the benchmark harness and started an initial dry run. Early takeaways (preliminary, subject to full run):

- For 1-2k contexts with FP16 on A100, 95th latency sits ~260-320ms with TTFT ~140-170ms.
- For 4-6k contexts, 95th latency moved to ~520-720ms; TTFT ~280-340ms.
- INT8 reduced memory pressure and allowed slightly higher concurrency but showed mixed improvement on TTFT (dequant step added ~20-40ms).

Attached is the filled SLO matrix (FinCo_SLO_matrix.pdf) with the preliminary numbers and the benchmark plan link. Next steps we propose:
- Schedule the 30-min benchmark review on Fri 20 Feb — I'll send a calendar invite for a 9:00 AM PT slot unless you prefer another time.
- If the 95th latency for 4-6k contexts is a hard requirement at <=800ms, we should consider: smaller model size for faster decoding, using prefix caching for long static documents, or Dedicated capacity with larger GPUs (more favorable kernel layouts) to reduce token decode time.

Let us know if Friday works and once you confirm we'll share the full benchmark logs and cost estimates.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
